question: In 1653, which French scientist observed that if some pressure is applied to any point of an incompressible fluid, the same pressure is transmitted to all points of the fluid and to the walls of the vessel?
solution:
Correct Answer **Blaise Pascal**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1653** **French scientist** who observed the principle you described is **Blaise Pascal.**
 
• This principle is known as **Pascal's law or the principle of transmission** of **fluid pressure.**
 
• **States that pressure **applied to an enclosed fluid is **transmitted uniformly** in **all directions throughout the fluid **and to the **walls of the container.**
 
• This principle has many practical applications, such as in **hydraulic systems and hydraulic lifts.**
 
• **Pascal's law** is one of the foundations of modern fluid mechanics and has had a significant impact on the fields of **engineering and physics.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** Daniel Bernoulli:

 
• **One of Bernoulli's most important** contributions to** fluid dynamics** was his** principle of conservation of energy,** which he formulated in **1738.**
 
• This **principle states** that as a fluid flows through a pipe, its total energy, consisting of its **potential energy (due to its position in a gravitational field) **and its** kinetic energy (due to its motion), remains constant. **

**Evangelista Torricelli:**

 
• **Evangelista Torricelli (1608-1647) **was an **Italian physicist and mathematician **who is best known for his **invention of the barometer** and his w**ork on the vacuum**
